chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-A'ala ibn Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Patience is to Faith as the head is to the body; so when the head is gone, the body is gone. Similarly, when patience is gone, Faith is gone.

key_terms.الرَّأْسُ: The head, used here as a metaphor for the most vital or controlling part.
key_terms.الصَّبْرُ: Patience, perseverance, or steadfastness in the face of adversity or divine command.
key_terms.الْإِيمَانُ: Faith, belief, or conviction in God and His teachings.
key_terms.الْجَسَدُ: The body, representing the whole entity that depends on the head.

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between patience and faith in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing patience not merely as a virtue but as the structural foundation of faith, akin to the head's role in the body. This analogy underscores the Shia scholarly view that *sabr* is the indispensable organ through which *iman* remains coherent and functional, implying that the loss of patience results in the collapse of one's spiritual integrity. The narration highlights the practical necessity of endurance in maintaining religious commitment amidst trials.
